notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first search did run, but my code crashed while printing the results, and then I hit my tool limit for this turn. So I read only the first few lines of one search result, and I didn't open any commentary pages. Since you asked me to report only what the pages say, I can't write the verse-by-verse notes yet.

**What I did find**

- **Overview of the chapter (vv. 1–22):** Matthew Henry's commentary describes the chapter as continuing the family lists of Judah. He calls Judah the largest and best-known of all the tribes. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_004.cfm

That's all. I can't say anything about the separate verses, the Protestant differences or the other views without reading the sources.

**Next time, I would cover:**

1. **Verse-by-verse sources for all 22 verses:** Enduring Word on 1 Chronicles 4, Matthew Henry (the page above), and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary notes on biblehub.com and studylight.org.
2. **vv. 9–10 (Jabez):** These two verses get the most attention and the most debate. I'd look at what Got Questions, Desiring God, Ligonier, Grace to You (gty.org) and The Gospel Coalition say about the prayer of Jabez. That includes their responses to Bruce Wilkinson's book *The Prayer of Jabez* and how it ties into prosperity teaching.
3. **v. 18 (Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, married to Mered):** what the older commentaries and the NET Bible notes say about her.
4. **Hard text spots:** NET Bible notes on the names and wording that are unclear in vv. 3, 13 and 17–22.
5. **Catholic and Orthodox views:** checks on newadvent.org and catholic.com, mainly for Jabez.

If you ask again, I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL for every point.
